detailed_rationale:
Cyient Ltd is an engineering R&D (ER&D) services company, with its Digital, Engineering & Technology (DET) segment - covering transportation, connectivity, sustainability, automotive and semiconductor engineering - making up roughly 79% of revenue, alongside a smaller Design-Led Manufacturing (DLM) electronics-manufacturing arm. FY26 revenue was roughly flat at Rs 7,268cr (vs Rs 7,360cr in FY25), but net profit fell 28.5% to Rs 463cr from Rs 648cr, with operating margin compressing from 15% to 12%. The quarterly trend is the real concern: profit has declined sequentially through the year, from Rs 157cr (Q1 FY26) down to Rs 109cr (Q4 FY26) - a steady erosion rather than a one-off dip.

This pattern is broadly consistent with sector-wide headwinds facing mid-cap ER&D/engineering-services vendors: softer discretionary tech and aerospace client budgets, pricing pressure from GenAI-driven productivity expectations, and increased competitive intensity. Cyient's valuation (P/E ~22-23x) is not stretched in absolute terms and its value_score in our model is actually favourable, and the balance sheet is effectively debt-free with strong cash generation historically - but a business with four consecutive quarters of declining profit is not, in our view, a 'statistically cheap, fundamentally sound' situation; it looks more like a genuine earnings downgrade cycle that the market has only partly priced in. A recent COO transition (new COO effective, prior COO departing September 2026) adds some near-term execution/leadership uncertainty on top of the operating headwinds.

The long-term ER&D demand backdrop (aerospace, medtech, semiconductor, renewable-energy engineering) remains structurally intact, but Cyient specifically is currently underperforming that backdrop, and we would want to see the profit decline stabilise before treating the cheap multiple as a genuine opportunity rather than a value trap.
recommendation_rationale: Four consecutive quarters of declining profit and margin compression outweigh the statistically cheap valuation - this reads as an earnings downgrade cycle rather than a bargain, so we are not rescuing despite the reasonable P/E and clean balance sheet.
summary: Cyient is an engineering services company whose profit has declined for four straight quarters even as revenue has held roughly flat, reflecting margin pressure across the mid-cap engineering-services sector. The stock's valuation is not expensive, but the earnings trend has been consistently negative, and a recent change in the company's chief operating officer adds some near-term uncertainty. We would want to see the profit decline stabilise before revisiting this name.
positive_para: Nearly debt-free balance sheet with historically strong cash generation; a reasonable valuation (~22-23x earnings) relative to the broader IT services sector; genuine structural demand tailwinds in aerospace, semiconductor, medtech and sustainability engineering that the company is positioned to serve over the long run.
negative_para: Net profit has declined in each of the last four reported quarters (from Rs 157cr to Rs 109cr), operating margin has compressed from 15% to 12%, and a leadership transition (new COO) adds execution uncertainty at a time when the business needs stabilising, not more change.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A cheap headline multiple is only a bargain if earnings are troughing; with profit declining sequentially for a full year, the current P/E does not yet look like a floor - it looks like a business still working through a downgrade cycle, so we would not underwrite the 'value' read at face value.
